source_verification_receipts.version: Management Science 69(7), 2023, pp. 3759–3777; publisher record, with arXiv:2009.00148v4 used only to inspect theorem text
source_verification_receipts.locator: Publisher abstract; corroborating arXiv v4 pp. 6 and 12–13, Assumption 2 and Theorem 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper is a one-unit design-based switchback framework with a fixed, given m-carryover order; its Theorem 2 gives an optimal regular geometry conditional on that order.
Assumption 2 imposes a specified m-carryover window and Theorem 2 gives a minimax optimal design under a multi-unit spillover/carryover model.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3; Corollaries 2–3 on p. 9 and Theorem 1 discussion on pp. 24 and 31
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies switchbacks under geometric mixing, deriving burn-in/block-length tradeoffs and geometric-bias error bounds rather than a fixed-array polynomial historical envelope.
The paper develops a modeled continuous-time switchback bias and MSE decomposition that includes carryover and correlated measurement-error components.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 4, Assumption 3 and Sections 3–4; p. 10, Theorem 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Assumption 3(a) rules out carryover and 3(b) permits only first-order carryover; the paper studies sequential rerandomization and corresponding asymptotic inference.
The paper models treatment and control as unknown Markov chains and characterizes consistent, asymptotically efficient likelihood-based adaptive policies under that stochastic model.

source_verification_receipts.version: Author preprint corresponding to Annals of Statistics 39(3), 2011, pp. 1608–1632, DOI 10.1214/11-AOS883
source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; publication metadata verified at DOI record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work introduces a data-driven bandwidth-selection rule with oracle inequalities and adaptive minimax density-estimation guarantees.
The paper proves constrained-risk inequalities for general losses, including nondecreasing losses applicable to absolute-loss lower-bound arguments.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a selected-design variance estimator plus a design-based limit-law and coverage statement for the multiscale selector, so the design becomes directly usable for inference as well as risk control.
Derive the sharp adaptation-index order by carrying out the stated policy-uniform constrained-risk lower-bound route, distinguishing bounded-cost adaptation from any unavoidable logarithmic penalty.
Add a short comparison corollary quantifying the rate difference between polynomial-envelope and geometric-mixing regimes at matched tail scales.

recommended_next_step: Advance this accepted flagship-eligible kernel to Stage 0 for derivation, retaining the sharp-adaptation question as the principal unresolved frontier.
